title: PRD: Schema contract tests and rollback gates for structured-output regressions
creator: Ibrahim Patel
description:
Summary: After a recent incident during a model routing rollout, downstream consumers experienced ingestion failures because a fallback model returned a subtly different structured output schema (renamed keys and optional fields removed). The postmortem identified gaps in our PRD and release process: we lack an automated contract test harness for structured outputs, rollout gates that validate schema compatibility, and a documented compatibility policy for transient model substitutions. This ticket updates the PRD to add schema-contract requirements, defines automated checks added to the release pipeline, and spells out rollback/mitigation criteria for schema-incompatible regressions.

Context and motivation:
- Incident snapshot: 2026-01-30 09:14 UTC — production traffic routed to backup model variant in us-east-1 due to capacity pressure. ~2% of requests returned a changed JSON shape in the "choices[].metadata" block, causing two major customers to drop requests and trigger error budgets.
- Root cause: the fallback model came from a different family that emits a compact metadata object by default. There was no automated compatibility check for structured output shapes during routing policy validation.
- Business impact: customer-facing ingestion errors, increased support tickets, and an emergency rollback that temporarily reduced regional capacity.

Goals for this PRD change:
1) Define a formal schema-compatibility contract for structured outputs (JSON Schema-ish) that all served models must advertise and validate against.
2) Add an automated contract test runner to CI that: validates sample outputs for every model variant against the declared contract, runs cross-variant compatibility checks, and fails pre-deploy if incompatibilities are detected.
3) Add a runtime synthetic verification step that runs a small set of canonical prompts through the routing fallback path during canary and autoscale events to detect schema drifts early.
4) Define rollback and mitigation acceptance criteria: when schema-incompatible responses exceed a threshold, trigger immediate routing rollback, notify customers, and open an incident runbook.
5) Update Console documentation and SDK helpers to expose stable adapter utilities that map deprecated keys to supported shapes for short-term compatibility.

Scope changes and trade-offs considered:
- Strict enforcement vs. pragmatic compatibility: We will require hard-fail in pre-deploy CI for changes to stable keys (major-version changes). For additive/optional fields we allow forward compatibility but add telemetry flags to monitor usage.
- Test coverage vs. deployment velocity: The test harness will run a prioritized subset of prompts for large model families to limit runtime; a full corpus run is optional and gated to nightly pipelines to avoid blocking urgent fixes.
- Runtime transformation vs. customer-side fixes: We will ship lightweight adapter utilities in SDKs to reduce customer impact for transient regressions but treat adapters as temporary mitigation, not a substitute for contract discipline.

Deliverables (what this ticket must produce):
- Updated PRD section "Structured Output Contract and Release Criteria" (Confluence link in links).
- Contract test runner added to runtime-model CI (GitHub action + test matrix).
- Canary synthetic check added to the serving control plane (configurable test bucket + threshold timers).
- Console UI flag and alert rule that surfaces schema compatibility regressions per-route and per-model.
- SDK adapter utility PR and short how-to doc for customers.

Acceptance Criteria:
acceptance_criteria: PRD text updated and reviewed: new section with compatibility policy, test requirements, and rollback thresholds; approved by Eng, DX (developer experience), and Legal for customer notification language.
Contract test runner added to model CI: for every model variant in the nightly matrix, the runner validates 50 canonical prompts against the declared schema and fails job on major-key mismatches.

Cross-variant compatibility check implemented: pre-deploy check that compares primary and fallback model output shapes and reports diffs to the release notes; must run in <10 minutes for prioritized families.

Canary synthetic verification integrated into control plane: when routing to a new variant or when fallback is used, a small probe suite runs and triggers a non-silent alert on >1% schema mismatch over 5 minutes.

Rollback automation: if schema-incompatible responses exceed configured thresholds, the system triggers an automated routing rollback and opens the incident runbook with pre-filled diagnostics (route, model IDs, recent samples).
Console and telemetry: per-route schema-compatibility dashboard updated; operators can see sample failing responses and the diff against expected contract within 5 minutes of detection.
SDK adapter shipped: helper function documented for customers to opt-in to temporary key-mapping with clear expiration guidance and telemetry for usage frequency.
Performance guardrails: contract checks and synthetic probes must not add >5% latency to request paths and must be configurable per-tenant to avoid noisy checks for latency-sensitive customers.
